title: Projects
description: |
  Our research on gender dysphoria, from a national cohort study to register-based epidemiology, qualitative interviews and open-source tools
---

When someone refers to gender identity, they usually mean the gender a person experiences themselves as and identifies with. That might be woman, man, neither, or something in between. People whose gender identity does not match the sex they were assigned at birth can experience severe discomfort and distress. That condition is called gender dysphoria.

Far more people have sought care for gender dysphoria over the past decade, particularly younger people, and they face a higher risk of poor mental and physical health, discrimination and violence. Most published research in the field is methodologically weak. Both the Swedish Agency for Health Technology Assessment and Assessment of Social Services (SBU) and the Swedish Research Council for Health, Working Life and Welfare (FORTE) have identified the resulting knowledge gaps and called for better studies.

We aim to answer several of those questions properly:

i. Is gender-affirming treatment associated with better outcomes in gender dysphoria, body satisfaction, mental health and social vulnerability, such as discrimination and exposure to violence?
ii. Do people undergoing gender-affirming treatment face a higher risk of physical outcomes, such as stroke and heart attack, or psychiatric outcomes, such as psychiatric admission and suicidal behaviour?
iii. What matters for people whose need for gender-affirming care changes, or who have experience of detransition, retransition or regret?

To answer them we combine three kinds of evidence. A large ongoing multicentre cohort study gives detailed, clinically meaningful measures. Register data covering everyone in Sweden with a gender dysphoria diagnosis gives the statistical power to assess rare but serious outcomes. Qualitative interviews explain the decisions behind the numbers.

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll('.project-card');
  let activeStatus = 'all';
  let activeTopic = 'all';

  function applyFilters() {
    cards.forEach(card => {
      const statusMatch = activeStatus === 'all' || card.dataset.status === activeStatus;
      const topics = JSON.parse(card.dataset.topics || '[]');
      const topicMatch = activeTopic === 'all' || topics.includes(activeTopic);
      card.style.display = (statusMatch && topicMatch) ? '' : 'none';
    });
  }

  document.querySelectorAll('.filter-status').forEach(btn => {
    btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      document.querySelectorAll('.filter-status').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
      activeStatus = btn.dataset.filter;
      btn.classList.add('active');
      applyFilters();
    });
  });

  document.querySelectorAll('.filter-topic').forEach(btn => {
    btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      document.querySelectorAll('.filter-topic').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
      activeTopic = btn.dataset.filter;
      btn.classList.add('active');
      applyFilters();
    });
  });
})();
</script>
```
